newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil up bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil up bargain hunting.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps rose at midday on Monday on bargain hunting as buyers came out after the market was sold down sharply on Friday, traders said.
"Fuel oil is up on some technical correction because of the big sell-off on Friday," one trader said.
September fuel oil swaps were last quoted up 25 cents from Friday at $103.75/$104.50 per tonne with October up 50 cents at $104.25/$105.00, brokers said.

Traders said market fundamentals are unchanged but all eyes are now focussed on the physical market where fresh bids and offers are expected to emerge after Friday's no show which led to the sell of the swaps market.
Supplies in Singapore, which were extremely tight, have since improved slightly following the arrival of several Middle East cargoes totalling over 250,000 tonnes, traders said.
Fuel oil output from Singapore refiners remained low due to the use of more light and middle-distillate rich crudes.
Gas oil swaps were steady in the absence of fresh indicators as concerns of a prompt physical overhang continue to loom over the market, traders said.
September was last quoted unchanged from Friday at $23.20/$23.30 per barrel, brokers said.
Traders said the steep contango is still making it worthwhile for oil companies to store their gas oil and jet fuel for winter.
But the current poor demand is forcing some to sell at big discounts in order to make room for fresh cargoes.
In the physical market, one 150,000-barrel cargo for September 2-6 lifting traded at $22.40 per barrel, free-on-board basis, down 10 cents from last Monday's traded level.
Jet fuel is also under pressure with the September regrade slipping to trade on Friday at 80 cents, lower than Thursday's $0.90/$1.10, brokers said.
September regrade was last quoted at 70-90 cents, they said.
